title: Stressed VaR and Market Risk Capital

maps.tested: Named by the handwritten sheet as an operational-risk-section calculation and reported in two exam recalls.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'stressed market VaR calc'; 'market risk capital charge calculations'; and a cross-domain item, 'mixed question: market risk stressed VaR, credit risk VaR given default rate.' That last one is a genuine cross-section integration vignette of the kind that resolves on one line of reasoning per option.

vardeezReading: ORR-22: untiered (the tier cell reads 0), but his themes 'Stressed market VaR (calculations)' and 'Basel 2.5 market risk calculation' land squarely here, so treat it as high priority. ORR-21: untiered, but his theme 'Basel III: three components and comparison with Basel I and II' draws on it.

los.vardeez: Stressed VaR calculation; Basel 2.5 market risk calculation

selectors.name: Stressed VaR term in Basel 2.5
selectors.what: The stressed VaR part of the Basel 2.5 charge: max(SVaR(t-1), ms x SVaR(avg)) with its own multiplier ms >= 3, added to the ordinary VaR term, with one-day figures scaled by sqrt(10). Includes the total MR(2.5) = max(VaR(t-1), mc x VaR(avg)) + max(SVaR(t-1), ms x SVaR(avg)).
selectors.theory: Why stressed VaR was added (historical-simulation VaR drifts down in calm periods and was slow to rise in 2007); how it is defined (the most stressful 250-day period in the last seven years for the current portfolio); why it changes little over time; why the Basel 2.5 charge is at least twice the 1996 charge when the multipliers are equal; why each max is a separate decision.

selectors.name: Market risk capital charge, 1996 Amendment
selectors.what: MR = max(VaR(t-1), m x VaR(avg)) with VaR(avg) the 60-day average, 10-day VaR = 1-day VaR x sqrt(10), and the multiplier m from the backtest: 5 or fewer exceptions in 250 days gives m = 3, 6 to 9 is at supervisory discretion, 10 or more requires m = 4. May continue to risk-weighted assets by multiplying capital by 12.5.
selectors.theory: The internal-models method of the 1996 Amendment: 10-day 99th percentile VaR, at least one year of daily data, why the multiplier term is usually the larger, why the previous day's VaR can exceed m times the average after a sharp position build-up, what an exception is, and how capital converts to RWA (x 12.5, the inverse of 8%).

selectors.name: Mixed vignette: market SVaR plus credit capital
selectors.what: A vignette combining the trading-book charge (10-day 99% VaR and stressed VaR with multipliers) and the banking-book credit capital at the 99.9th percentile default rate, capital = sum of EAD x LGD x (DR99.9 - PD), computed separately and then added; each option carries one error.
selectors.theory: The two charges follow different conventions (10-day 99% with multipliers versus one-year 99.9% net of EL) and are added only afterwards; capital covers unexpected loss only because reserves cover EL, so the undeducted 99.9th percentile loss is Hull's credit VaR, not the capital; the usual planted errors are dropping SVaR, dropping a multiplier, forgetting sqrt(10), and forgetting to subtract EL.

notSelected: ORR-22 b (the incremental risk charge: default charge at the IRB 99.9th percentile, extension to rating changes, constant credit quality, three-month liquidity horizon) and ORR-22 c (the comprehensive risk charge and its securitization percentages) carry only a bare 'Basel 2.5' pointer and no shape or Map point, so they are left to their definitions; ORR-21 c's standardized method, specific risk, Tier 3 capital and qualitative criteria carry no shape.
